calls.summary:
# Usage-Based Pricing & Positioning discussion
Date: 2026-09-29 | Duration: 36m

## Summary
The team agreed to manage CDN costs case by case, using them flexibly in negotiations rather than as a primary revenue source. Mobile and front-end SDKs drive most CDN requests, while bandwidth costs increase with larger feature-flag payloads and many simultaneous experiments. Enterprise deals will typically include about 1 GB of bandwidth per million CDN requests, with overages handled retroactively. Managed event warehousing will have a floor of about $5 per million events and may support volumes from hundreds of millions to a billion events monthly. Event forwarding will offer a lower-cost, flexible option but is less sticky because clients can rebuild it quickly; real-time monitoring is planned to improve retention. The team also proposed a calculator using monthly active users or event volume to bundle CDN, bandwidth, forwarding, and event usage into simpler packages. AI token pricing remains under consideration, likely with a markup of about 20% over provider rates.

## Keywords
CDN requests, event pricing, bandwidth costs, event forwarder, AI tokens, pricing calculator

## Action Items

**Jeremy Dorn**
Share the presentation/deck with the team for reference (26:18)
Collaborate with Dan Wathne to build a pricing calculator based on monthly active users or session data for pricing traffic-related usage components (25:29)

**Dan Wathne**
Begin work on building a pricing calculator that maps customer MAU and event usage to pricing levels, informed by prior work at Statsig (23:08)

**All Sales Team**
Collect feedback from enterprise prospects regarding their AI budget planning for next fiscal year to inform sales strategy and pricing positioning (22:38)
